selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main meaning of the Arabic sentence in this passage?
questions.answer: It means that the ending of their prayer or call is praise to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: What act of worship is at the center of this short passage?
questions.answer: Praising Allah.

questions.question: At what stage does this praise come, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It comes at the end.

questions.question: What does calling Allah the Lord of all worlds show about His relationship to creation?
questions.answer: It shows that He is the Owner, Sustainer, and Ruler of everything.

questions.question: Does the passage point to praise for one group only or for all creation? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: It points to all creation, because Allah is described as the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: What belief about Allah is affirmed by the phrase “Lord of all worlds”?
questions.answer: It affirms His universal lordship over every world and every creature.

questions.question: In simple American English, what does this passage say?
questions.answer: It says that the final thing they say is praise to Allah, the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: Who is being praised in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What title of Allah appears in the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: What does the word “final” add to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that praise remains at the conclusion and is not something secondary.

questions.question: If Allah is the Lord of all worlds, what does that imply about His care and authority?
questions.answer: It implies that His care and authority reach everything, not just one place or people.

questions.question: Is the focus of the passage on asking for something or honoring Allah?
questions.answer: It is on honoring Allah.

questions.question: What is the core message of this one-line passage?
questions.answer: The core message is that the conclusion of one’s supplication or call should be praise to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how speech should end?
questions.answer: It should end with glorifying and thanking Allah.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s name followed by a title related to all worlds?
questions.answer: To show that the praise belongs to the One who sustains and governs everything.

questions.question: What does this statement teach about the scope of Allah’s lordship?
questions.answer: His lordship is universal and includes all realms of creation.

questions.question: What relationship between prayer and praise appears here?
questions.answer: Praise is shown as a fitting conclusion to prayer.

questions.question: What is emphasized more here: information about creation or devotion to the Creator?
questions.answer: Devotion to the Creator.

questions.question: What is being described as the last part of their call or prayer?
questions.answer: Praising Allah.

questions.question: Which name or attribute of Allah in the passage makes the praise universal?
questions.answer: The title that describes Him as the Lord of all worlds.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the right response of believers at the close of worship?
questions.answer: They should turn to praise and thankfulness to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage not limit Allah to one nation or one place?
questions.answer: Because it describes Him in a way that includes every world.

questions.question: What does this line show about the importance of praise in Islam?
questions.answer: It shows that praise is central enough to stand at the end of one’s prayerful words.

questions.question: How does the passage combine belief and worship in a few words?
questions.answer: It declares who Allah is and responds to Him with praise.
